title: Exact Transfer of Bounded Linear Recovery and Relative Weight Hierarchies
description: For a represented inner code and a fixed target set, this preprint associates a nested pair of helper codes and identifies its relative generalized Hamming weights with the exact minimum helper-union costs for recovering target subspaces of each dimension. It proves that, in concatenations whose outer dual distance tends to infinity, the sharp eventual confinement threshold is the corresponding relative generalized Hamming weight plus the inner dual distance. Below that threshold, zero-extension preserves every bounded normalized recovery equation and its exact helper support. Consequences include a best-target generalized-weight identity, MDS threshold rigidity, positive-density realization in asymptotically good fixed-alphabet families, and transfer of bounded service-rate regions. Separations show that the complete relative-weight hierarchy does not determine bounded repair reliability and that different coefficient presentations of the same nested pair can have different confinement thresholds. A projective-simplex family gives an explicit non-MDS hierarchy and projective-rank reliability law.
